summary: Measures that protect data and computer systems — physical security, firewalls, encryption, biometrics and anti-virus protection — and using backups and disk mirroring.

theory.title: Protection measures for data and computer systems

items.title: Protection against physical risks
items.content: Locked server rooms, CCTV, ID cards; UPS against power cuts; fire alarms and extinguishers; air conditioning; off-site backups against fire and flood.

items.title: Firewalls (inter-network screens)
items.content: Filter traffic between a network and the Internet using rules on IP addresses, ports and protocols; block unauthorised access and suspicious outgoing connections.

items.title: Encryption
items.content: Scrambles data with a **key** so that intercepted or stolen data cannot be read without the key. Used for Wi-Fi (WPA3), websites (HTTPS/TLS), disks (BitLocker), messages.

items.title: Biometrics
items.content: Identify a person by unique **physical characteristics**: fingerprint, face, iris, voice. Cannot be forgotten or easily shared.

items.title: Anti-virus / anti-malware
items.content: Detects, quarantines and removes malicious programs; real-time scanning; must be updated.

blocks.title: Symmetric vs asymmetric encryption
rows: A **public key** encrypts; only the matching **private key** decrypts
The key must be shared securely
Solves key sharing — the public key can be given to anyone
RSA in HTTPS key exchange, digital signatures

blocks.title: Caesar cipher — the simplest symmetric cipher (shift 3)
blocks.content: `HELLO` → `KHOOR`. The **key** is the shift. Modern ciphers are far stronger, but the idea is the same: without the key the text is unreadable.

rows: Unique to each person; cannot be forgotten or lost
Can be affected by injuries, dirt, lighting, illness
**Cannot be changed** if the biometric data is stolen
Privacy concerns about storing biometric data

blocks.title: Authentication factors
rows: Phone (SMS code, authenticator app), smart card, key fob

blocks.content: **Two-factor authentication (2FA)** combines two different factors (e.g. password + SMS code), so a stolen password alone is not enough.

items.title: Backup
items.content: A copy of the data made **at intervals** and stored separately (external disk, NAS, cloud, another site). Can restore **older versions**.

items.title: Disk mirroring (RAID 1)
items.content: Every write goes to **two disks at once**; if one disk fails, the other continues **immediately**.

blocks.title: A backup strategy for a school
rows: Incremental every night, full every Sunday
Little data lost; fast nightly backups
Encrypted cloud storage + an external disk off-site
Can go back to before a ransomware attack
Restore a test file every month
A backup that cannot be restored is useless
No downtime if a disk fails

blocks.content: Mirroring **copies mistakes instantly** — a deleted or encrypted (ransomware) file is lost on both disks. Only a **backup** protects against that.
